questionsToConsider: Are you reviewing one page or the whole site, and should reviewers name the page each time?
Which parts of the design are still open to change, and which are already signed off?
Do you want feedback from real visitors as well as stakeholders, and should their answers be read separately?
Who decides between conflicting comments when two reviewers want opposite things?
guide.howToUseResponses: Group the answers by reviewer type before reading them, because a stakeholder and a first-time visitor are judging different things. Start with anyone who could not tell what the page is for: that is a message problem, and no amount of polish fixes it. Use the ranking to agree the order of work, and treat the specific change requests as a checklist for the next round.
customizeSteps: Rename the rows in the rating grid to the parts of your design that are genuinely up for review.
Prefill the page link with a hidden field when you send one link per page, so reviewers skip the first question.
Share the link along with the preview, and set a date by which you need the comments.

faqs.q: What should a website design feedback form ask?
faqs.a: Whether the page's purpose is clear, how readable and easy to navigate it is, and which specific changes the reviewer wants. Asking reviewers to rank changes stops every comment from looking equally urgent.

faqs.q: How do I get useful feedback on a website design?
faqs.a: Ask specific questions about purpose, readability and navigation instead of "what do you think?", and ask reviewers to point to the section they mean. A screenshot upload helps too.

faqs.q: Can clients attach screenshots with their feedback?
faqs.a: Yes. The form has an optional upload for images or a PDF, so a reviewer can mark up the design and send it along with their answers.

faqs.q: Can I share this form with people outside my team?
faqs.a: Yes. Share it as a link or embed it on a page, and every response lands in your dashboard, where you can also export it to CSV.

doc.title: Website design feedback
doc.description: Structured comments on a page design, ranked by what should change first.

blocks.title: Thanks for looking over the new design. A few quick questions and your comments will be in one tidy place.
Which page are you reviewing?
blocks.description: Paste the link to the page or the design preview.

blocks.title: What was your first impression of the page?
Within a few seconds, could you tell what this page is for?
What did you think it was for, and what threw you off?
How does the design do on each of these?
How easy was it to find what you were looking for?
Put these in order of what should change first.
Which specific changes would you like to see?
blocks.description: Point to the section if you can, for example "the pricing table" or "the footer".

blocks.title: Want to attach a marked-up screenshot?
Would you like a call to talk the changes through?
What's the best email to arrange that?

endings.title: Thanks for the review
endings.bodyMd: Your comments go straight to the designer, and you'll see the changes in the next round.

endings.title: Let's talk it through 📞
endings.bodyMd: We'll email you to find a time, and bring your notes to the call.
